clue.text: Carpenter in fast food outlet

definitions.meaning: British slang for a carpenter or joiner

explanation.surface: A woodworker spotted working at a burger bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word joining the two definitions. Both senses are everyday British slang: a woodworker, and a fish-and-chip shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are British slang: one for a joiner, the other for a shop selling fried fish with chips.

clue.text: Flighty workers hailed taxi in English town

indicators.note: something hailed is called out, so these words are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a cab in Crewe, a railway town in Cheshire, England

explanation.surface: Someone flags down a cab somewhere in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hailed' looks like part of taking a taxi, but it signals that 'cab in Crewe' is spoken aloud. CREWE is a railway town in Cheshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff who serve passengers aboard an aircraft work in flight, hence the playful adjective 'flighty'.

clue.text: Upset at siren going off

indicators.note: a siren going off is set loose, so its letters with the word at are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed by an alarm sounding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' reads as the siren sounding, but it signals an anagram of AT SIREN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone weeping is visibly distressed, so this phrase means emotionally upset.

clue.text: Friend enlisting tenant, perhaps, one involved with Bush's campaign?

indicators.note: to enlist is to take someone into your ranks, so the word for friend takes other letters inside it

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a tenant is one example of a resident, signalled by 'perhaps'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A friend recruits a lodger for a US election drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enlisting' signals a container. The question mark flags that Bush's campaign is only one example of the adjective: any White House race fits.
explanation.definitionFit: George W. Bush ran for the highest office in the US, so his campaign was for the White House.

clue.text: stretch of water

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'stretch of water (3,3)': only the definition survives; the wordplay is cut short and a search found no full text

clue.text: Transport drug

definitions.meaning: a transport is a state of overwhelming joy or rapture
a common name for the recreational drug MDMA

explanation.surface: A two-word note about moving narcotics around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like a verb about carrying, but here it is a noun meaning rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapture or bliss is one sense; the other is the street name of the stimulant MDMA.

clue.text: Jazz music be hanged!

definitions.meaning: a style of big-band jazz of the 1930s

explanation.surface: A grumpy listener damns jazz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be hanged!' reads as an oath dismissing jazz, but it is a second definition: to swing is to die on the gallows.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the 1930s big-band style; the other is old slang for execution by rope.

clue.text: Member of resistance group beheaded worker

indicators.note: losing the head means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a partisan is a member of an armed resistance movement

explanation.surface: A resistance fighter is executed by decapitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' removes the first letter, P, from PARTISAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual craftsman is a type of worker.

clue.text: See tot play endlessly

indicators.note: without its end means the last letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a drama is a play

explanation.surface: Watch a toddler acting in a show with no end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a small child but is a small measure of spirits. 'endlessly' drops the last A of DRAMA; 'See' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of whisky or other spirit is a tot.

clue.text: Reply in court about introduction of bail, say

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A response in a hearing on whether to grant bail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduction of' takes B, the first letter of 'bail'.
explanation.definitionFit: In old English pleading, this was a defendant's answer to the plaintiff's surrejoinder.

clue.text: Help relative, in a way

indicators.note: the relative word goes inside the abbreviation for a way

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
sis is short for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: Giving aid to a family member in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' reads as 'somewhat', but 'in' is a container signal and 'way' is the street abbreviation; A stands as written in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid someone is to support them.

clue.text: In the afternoon, mail man receives one awful upset

parts.note: post is mail

indicators.note: the word for man takes the following letters inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
dire means awful

explanation.surface: A postman is handed something that badly distresses him one afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses its two pieces as one run (in a down clue the letters go upward), and 'receives' signals a container round them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase behind the abbreviation p.m. means after midday.

clue.text: Maiden ordering bananas, surprisingly, not British fruit

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: the fodder letters are rearranged in an unexpected order
the letter for British is taken away from the fodder

explanation.surface: A young woman orders bananas, unexpectedly not British ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' is M, from cricket scoring. 'not British' drops B from ORDERING BANANAS, and 'surprisingly' scrambles what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: These small loose-skinned citrus fruits, such as tangerines, are a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Survey work in gold mine?

definitions.meaning: a survey is a view or outlook over a scene
to search the ground for gold or other minerals

explanation.surface: Mapping work at a gold mine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second definition as a playful description of digging for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide view counts as one sense; the other is searching land for mineral deposits.

clue.text: Desire to tour Middle Eastern republic

indicators.note: touring something means going all round it, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire
ME is an abbreviation for Middle Eastern

explanation.surface: Wanting to travel round a country in Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle Eastern' looks like part of the definition, but it is an abbreviation that sits inside the word for desire, which 'to tour' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The country on the southern tip of Arabia is a republic.

clue.text: Rumble one creating trouble for PM once

indicators.note: a trouble-maker stirs things up, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: fodder for the anagram

explanation.surface: Someone who sees through a troublemaker who plagued a former premier.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Melbourne was a 19th-century British Prime Minister. 'creating trouble' signals an anagram of RUMBLE ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Viscount Melbourne was Queen Victoria's first Prime Minister.

clue.text: Writer's humble wish only partly expressed

indicators.note: only a portion of the words is spoken, so the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: An author's modest hope, voiced only in part.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'humbLE WISh'. C. S. Lewis is the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: C. S. Lewis, author of the Narnia books, is a writer.

clue.text: Indian city having good fortune these days

parts.note: luck is good fortune
now means at present

explanation.surface: A place in India currently enjoying good luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Uttar Pradesh is a city in northern India.

clue.text: Prolong quick trip abroad?

parts.note: a spin is a short drive or outing
out means out of doors or away

explanation.surface: Stretch out a short jaunt overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' here means away from home, giving OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag something out is to make it last longer.

clue.text: Those people hold girl back in part of Greece

indicators.note: the word for those people holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: they means those people

indicators.note: back means the word for girl is read in reverse

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Some people restrain a girl in a Greek region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for girl and 'hold' signals a container; Those people are the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Thessaly is a region of central Greece.

clue.text: Evil prophet loudly claiming to be genuine

parts.note: sin is evil or wrongdoing

indicators.note: said out loud, so the word for prophet is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: A wicked soothsayer proclaims his honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loudly' makes SEER be heard as CERE. 'claiming to be' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being honest and heartfelt is being real, not feigned.

clue.text: Security device commander has to keep one lot of people in building

parts.note: Com. is an abbreviation for commander

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so the building word contains the next pieces

parts.note: a block is a building
I is the Roman numeral for one
a nation is a large body of people

explanation.surface: An officer must guard a group of people inside a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to keep' puts I NATION inside BLOCK, after COM, the abbreviation for commander.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock opened by dialling a number sequence is a security device.

clue.text: Child eating small portion of rib joint

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the word for child surrounds a letter

parts.note: a mite is a small child

indicators.note: a small portion here is just the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A youngster chewing a bit of a spare rib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small portion of rib' gives R, and 'eating' puts it inside MITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworking joint with a 45-degree bevel, as on a picture frame, is a mitre joint.

clue.text: Hold spy up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to peek is to look furtively, to spy

explanation.surface: Detain an agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spy' looks like a noun but is a verb, PEEK, which 'up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain something is to keep it.

clue.text: I could be taken in by unacceptable idea

indicators.note: being taken in means going inside, so I goes into the phrase for unacceptable

parts.note: 'not on' is a British phrase for unacceptable

explanation.surface: Someone fears being fooled by an outrageous concept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on' is everyday British for unacceptable. 'could be taken in by' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A concept or belief is an idea.

clue.text: Fruit supplier's deceptive statement about a certain measure

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for a deceptive statement goes round the measure

parts.note: a lie is a deceptive statement
a metre is a measure of length

explanation.surface: A fruit seller lies about weights and measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts METRE inside LIE. The 's of 'supplier's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree bearing citrus fruit supplies it; the linden is also so called.

clue.text: Flowers on grave desecrated in the war

indicators.note: desecrated means violated or defiled, so the letters of the words are broken up

explanation.surface: Graveside blooms vandalised during wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desecrated' signals an anagram of THE WAR; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of blooms laid as a tribute at a burial or memorial.

clue.text: Sounds like an old building

indicators.note: signals that the words are heard, not spelt

parts.note: an ex is an old partner, so ex stands for old

explanation.surface: Something resembling an ancient structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an old' said aloud is 'an ex', heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension or outbuilding added to a main structure.
